final_message:
You're right: the dip is almost entirely three ports. It only shows up in **Q2 2024**, though. Q2 2023 (13,036 TEU) was in line with the quarters around it.

**Q2 2024 compared with the average of the other 2024 quarters (TEU):**

| Port | Q2 2024 | Other quarters avg | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ivelholm | 375 | 1,784 | −1,409 |
| Fennick | 366 | 1,752 | −1,386 |
| Brackwater | 466 | 1,697 | −1,231 |
| The other 7 ports | — | — | +878 net |
| **Total** | 9,622 | 12,770 | **−3,148** |

- **Those three ports make up all of the dip and more.** Together they're down about 4,000 TEU, which is roughly 128% of the total gap. The other seven ports are flat or up, mainly Cindervale (+457), Dovesend (+309) and Juniper Reach (+278), and that partly cancels the drop. Shipment value follows the same pattern.
- **It starts and stops on the quarter boundaries.** Across the three ports there were 22 shipments in March and 21 in July, but only 5 in each of April, May and June. Their TEU fell about 75–80% in that window.
- **It hit every carrier type**, not one segment. Container shipments fell from 40 to 9, bulk from 16 to 5, and tanker from 5 to 1.

**One caveat:** a drop that lines up exactly with the quarter and recovers fully afterwards looks less like a real disruption to trade. It looks more like a reporting gap, such as a data feed that went down or records not loaded for those ports. You'd want to rule that out before treating it as a real slowdown. If the three ports share a system or operator, that would point to missing data. The rise at the other ports could be real cargo that was rerouted, so check whether it's that or just noise.

I ran this with standalone polars scripts and haven't changed `notebooks/explore.py`. I can add these breakdowns and a port-by-quarter chart to the notebook if you want.

import polars as pl
pl.Config.set_tbl_rows(100); pl.Config.set_tbl_cols(20)
df=pl.read_csv('data/shipments.csv',try_parse_dates=True).filter(pl.col('ship_date').dt.year()==2024).with_columns(q=pl.col('ship_date').dt.quarter(),m=pl.col('ship_date').dt.month())
p=df.group_by('port','q').agg(teu=pl.col('teu').sum())
base=p.filter(pl.col('q')!=2).group_by('port').agg(base=pl.col('teu').mean())
q2=p.filter(pl.col('q')==2).join(base,on='port').with_columns(gap=pl.col('teu')-pl.col('base')).sort('gap')
print(q2.with_columns(share=pl.col('gap')/pl.col('gap').sum()))
three=['Brackwater','Fennick','Ivelholm']
print(df.filter(pl.col('m').is_between(3,7)).with_columns(g=pl.col('port').is_in(three)).group_by('g','m').agg(teu=pl.col('teu').sum(),n=pl.len()).sort('g','m'))
print(df.filter(pl.col('port').is_in(three),pl.col('q')==2).sort('ship_date'))
print(df.filter(pl.col('port').is_in(three)).group_by('carrier_type','q').agg(n=pl.len()).sort('carrier_type','q'))
"
